title: Garner versus Tatum as accompanists for his solos
summary: Garner improvised and accompanied Stewart's solos with room to breathe, while Tatum tended to play all over the piano.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How did you find him in terms of improvising? Did you find him to be an improviser?
Did you find him to improvise more than Tatum or about as -- about equal?
I don't mean quality. I just mean did he have as many routines that he --

Oh, he had -- we had a few routines, routines, and improvisation was a prominent thing with us, you know. We had lots of fun improvising, and at times I noticed that, like when I was playing with Tatum, here's a point I'd like to bring out. When I was taking a solo, bass solo, at times Tatum would not knowingly, possibly, he would kind of

drown me out, not meaningly, but his style of playing piano, I'd be trying to take a solo, and Tatum would be soloing also along with me, and at times that was a little bit perturbing to me, you know, until I got used to it, which didn't happen in the case of Erroll Garner,
In fact Erroll accompanied me in a way where he wouldn't get in my way when I was soloing, you know. He'd give me a beautiful accompaniment.
He'd give you more breathing room?
Tatum wasn't -- accompanying wasn't his forte?
That wasn't -- some of those things with Norman Granz ---
You heard them, some of those recordings where someone else would be taking the solo, for instance, myself taking the solo. Tatum would be all over the piano.
